claim_one_line: THE HANDOFFS I WROTE INTO BUT HAD NOT READ. B1052 wrote a handoff into docs/handoffs/ after opening TWENTY-TWO LINES of one of the two files already there, purely to copy the seat-to-seat convention -- NEITHER WAS READ, and the campaign's own step is 'read every doc in docs/'. That directory holds NEGATIVES_HUNT_HANDOFF_2026-07-21.md, an OWNER-DIRECTED FULL-REPO SCRUTINY BRIEF ('scrutinize the whole repo -- is everything calculated properly, have we made mistakes?') whose remit overlaps this refresh's directly, and PHYSICS_PATHFINDER_PROMPT_2026-07-21.md, its declared companion. THE GAP SURFACED BECAUSE THE OWNER ASKED WHETHER THE HANDOFFS WERE MINE, NOT BECAUSE I CHECKED. Reading them found three things. ONE, THE HUNT RAN -- B742 (P1: 213 banked negatives triaged to 162 true to 33 P1, two revivals), B745 (cross-verified both), B754 (P2, the spectral face), B765 (P3, depth), B770 (the closure census); stated plainly because a standing owner directive left unexecuted would have been the more dramatic finding and would have been WRONG. TWO, ITS P4 STRATUM HAS NO ARC: the handoff names four strata and describes the last as 'the early era (pre-B300) ... Oldest = least anatomy = HIGHEST PRIOR OF A BURIED POSITIVE', while B770's census summarises the execution as 'P1-P3' and no arc's claim line claims an early-era stratum -- and PRE-B300 IS EXACTLY THE REGION B1050/B1051 JUST CLOSED, on a different axis. THREE, AND IT LANDS ON MY OWN ARC: THE SIX ARCS B1050 RESTORED AS A WALL WERE STRUCTURALLY INVISIBLE TO THAT HUNT. It selected BANKED NEGATIVES; B19, B21, B28, B30, B34 and B35 all carry arc_verdict PROVED over bodies reading STALLED, and their atlas statuses are `banked` or `open` -- NEVER `dead`, the hunt's primary hunting ground -- so neither selection surface could see them, and NONE OF THE SIX APPEARS ANYWHERE IN THE HUNT'S ARCS. THIS IS L166's DEFECT WITH A FAR LARGER CONSEQUENCE THAN L166 STATED: L166 priced it as reader confusion, someone tracing B16 meeting PROVED over a body saying STALLED, but THE REAL COST IS THAT FOURTEEN ARCS WERE SKIPPED BY A REPO-WIDE OWNER-DIRECTED AUDIT, because both surfaces it selected on say something other than 'negative'. Registered in L166, where it materially strengthens option 3 (repair the metadata), which remains the owner's call. AND THE HUNT KNEW THE SHAPE FIRST: B742 flagged '51 atlas-miner mis-classes' from its own status heuristic -- the same defect family from the other side, three hundred arcs earlier, this refresh's recurring lesson (a record describes its own era) arriving once more. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM: it does not claim the wall is wrong, since B1050's six are STALLED rather than kills and the row's scope is 'does not DERIVE the selector', a statement about routes tried and exactly the posture the pathfinder brief's hatch table asks for; what IS claimed is that the repo's own blade for pre-B300 negatives has never been applied to them, and the row now says so. FOUR ATTEMPTS TO PROVE A NEGATIVE, AND THE FOURTH WAS TO STOP: establishing 'P4 has no arc' wrongly matched loop4/qp4 directory names, then B401's 'P4 - the exact-identity dossier' and B570's 'AP4' and B737's 'P4 - KMS', then the hunt's own CITATION of B737's P4 -- because P4 CARRIES AT LEAST FOUR DISTINCT MEANINGS IN THIS CORPUS plus two filename collisions, which is the E1 vocabulary-drift class (the error this refresh named as its most expensive recurring one) ARRIVING INSIDE THE ARC THAT REPORTS IT. So the claim rests on two documents stating it directly -- the handoff NAMES a fourth stratum, the census WRITES 'P1-P3' -- and the four false-positive families are named in the checks so the narrowing is auditable rather than a silent retreat. Third over-broad pattern in two arcs, and each time the fix was the same: ask the precise question, and test both directions. 30 checks; 28 gates green; Gate 5 untouched; nothing to CLAIMS.md.
